task: Per-frame Barrett's neoplasia likelihood from stacked endoscopy frames

architecture.backbone: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 with 4 register tokens, self-supervised pretraining on gastrointestinal endoscopy imagery, input resolution 336
architecture.adaptation: LoRA (r=32, alpha=64, dropout=0.1) on the attention qkv projections, merged into the backbone weights for deployment
architecture.pooling: Attention-based multiple-instance pooling over patch tokens (Ilse et al., ICML 2018, Eq. 8): a two-layer scorer (768 -> 128 -> 1) rates each of the 576 patch tokens, scores are softmax-normalised across patches into weights, and the frame embedding is their weighted sum
architecture.head: Single linear layer on the pooled 768-dimensional embedding

training.optimizer: AdamW, learning rate 3.62e-4, weight decay 3.96e-5, cosine schedule, mixed precision
training.augmentation: Horizontal/vertical flip, 90-degree rotation, mild affine, mild brightness and contrast

ensemble.combination: Arithmetic mean of the per-frame sigmoid outputs

inference.granularity: Each frame is scored independently; the output for a frame depends only on that frame and is unaffected by input batching
inference.output: One neoplasia likelihood in [0, 1] per input frame
